item.title: River Systems Field Class — Fri Oct 23, 11:00 AM
item.description: River Systems Field Class with Anton DuMars Friday, October 23 | 11am – 5pm BRN – Core Register Here! For the River Systems Field Experience, we will observe processes and indicators along the Davidson River, a Blue Ridge tributary of the French Broad catchment basin. We consider channel hierarchy (first order, second order, etc.). Our stops include observation and discussions of flow and flood indicators and river forms, such as cut banks, point bars, and flood channels. We observe sediment texture, sediment load, and consider sediment source. This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, let us know and we will tell you where to meet. This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. item.description: Spring Starts in the Winter for Roses with John Smith Friday, October 23 | 1 – 3pm BREG – Elective Register Here! Planning a great rose garden doesn’t begin in spring, the work begins with thoughtful planning through the quiet days of winter. Every hour spent preparing now is rewarded with healthier plants and more time to enjoy your garden in the spring. During this class learn best practices, tips and tricks, and other work that goes into planning and maintaining a great rose garden. This class is part of a series of offerings in collaboration with the Asheville Blue Ridge Rose Society as part of their Rose Grower’s School. John Smith is a Past President of Asheville- Blue Ridge Rose Society and is a Certified Consulting Rosarian for the American Rose Society since 2010. He has been growing roses since 1979 in New Jersey, California and now in North Carolina. item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Oct 24, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: Backyard Baskets: Coiling with Natural Materials — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM
item.description: Backyard Baskets: Coiling with Natural Materials with Alyssa Sacora Wednesday, October 28 | 10 – 4pm Register Here! Many local plants lend themselves to basket making. In this workshop, we will create a coiled vessel using leaves and grasses harvested from cultivated gardens and wild places. Coiling is a hand-stitching process that transforms a continuous bundle of fibers into a strong and versatile container. Found in cultures worldwide, it is a beautiful technique to create one-of-a-kind baskets from plants growing in your backyard. Participants can choose to complete a small basket in class or leave with extra materials to continue their basket at home. Coiling is great for beginner basket makers and those with weaving experience that want to learn more about using local plants in their creative practice. item.title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum — Sat Nov 7, 9:30 AM — Asheville Art Museum
item.description: Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibits. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. Join Joshua on 8/22, 10/3, 11/7, and 12/5. Joshua Cant

item.title: Bent Creek-Sidehill: 7 mi 1000 ft elev. gain — Fri Oct 9, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign-up opens Sunday, Oct. 4th, 8:00 pm]**
This is a "Todd Hike" that's mostly on Lower Sidehill Trail and South Ridge Rd. It's a pretty area deep into Bent Creek. The plan is for a "lollipop" with a short stem at the start and finish, and a big loop the rest of the way.
Be prepared for a moderate pace, around 2.4 mph. There's good footing throughout, with a combination of forest trails and gravel roads. Ups and downs are relatively mild. If you're on the fence about poles, you probably won't need them here. Bring water and, if you're inclined, a snack, too. There'll be a little break somewhere around the middle.
**CARPOOLING TIME & PLACE**
There's limited trailhead parking, so we'll carpool from the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House (directions below). Look for me and my silver Hyundai. Come early to allow for traffic. We'll depart by 9:00 AM
